Mike (Sales): Heads-up — Large payments customer (FinSolve) just surfaced dedicated capacity ask. They want predictable latency for embeddings + generation, with big burst windows during batch jobs and end-of-day settlement windows. Need rough sizing + a recommended autoscale strategy.
Ana (Product): Thanks. What load numbers did they give? SLO targets? any model preferences?
Mike (Sales): From the call: steady traffic ~300 qps (mixed embeddings + gen), bursts to ~1500 qps for 10–20 minutes, and nightly batch spikes for 45m. Tail latency target 99p < 500ms for gen responses; embeddings can tolerate 200ms 99p. They're ok with a smaller model if latency improved, but want quality parity w current open-70B-ish.
Jordana (Solutions): Quick clarifying Qs: what's average response size for gen (tokens out) and embedding dims? Also are those qps numbers per endpoint or aggregate across many routes?
Mike (Sales): Gen avg output ~180 tokens. Embeddings: 768-dim, each request small. Numbers are aggregate across product (several routes) but we can map to separate pools if needed.
Kevin (Eng-Platform): Top-level thoughts: we should propose a reserved baseline pool for steady 300 qps and a burst pool that can scale up on policy. For estimation I need tokens/sec target: 300 * 180 = 54k tokens/sec baseline, burst 1500 * 180 = 270k tokens/sec.
Emily (C-S): Customer will want cost predictability — recommend commit for baseline and on-demand burst credits. Also they need audit logs and fallbacks for P0 app flows.
Kevin (Eng-Platform): Benchmark numbers (approx): quantized 70B on our A100-style nodes: single GPU sustained ~15k tokens/sec at production batching patterns. With aggressive batching maybe 20k, but tail suffers. So baseline 54k / 15k ~= 4 GPUs. For burst 270k / 15k ~= 18 GPUs. So plan: reserved pool 4 GPUs, autoscale max up to 24 GPUs (gives headroom) with burst billing.
Ana (Product): Nice. Can we satisfy 99p < 500ms with that? 70B quantized at high batch sizes still has tail risk.
Kevin (Eng-Platform): For 99p latency we should route high-priority gen to a latency-optimized variant (e.g., distilled 13B or 35B quantized) which gives much better latency per GPU. Propose smart routing: 60% of gen at baseline to 70B for quality, 40% to 35B for latency-sensitive endpoints. That lowers tokens/sec demand on 70B pool.
Jordana (Solutions): If we route some percent to 35B, re-calc: assume 70B handles 180 * 0.6 * 300 = 32.4k tokens/sec baseline -> ~3 GPUs. Burst similarly reduces. Also cost/cost-per-token improves.
Kevin (Eng-Platform): Autoscale policy stub:
```
- reserved_capacity: 4 gpus (70B pool)
- burst_max: 24 gpus
- scale_out_threshold: 70% GPU utilization
- scale_in_cooldown: 180s
- scale_out_concurrency_window: 30s
- burst_grace_period: allow 10 minute sustained burst before force-throttle/billing
- fallback_routes: send overflow to 35B pool or queued responses
```
Mike (Sales): Customer will want a nominal monthly committed baseline and per-minute burst pricing. Also they'd ask about cold start when scaling — how fast do GPUs become ready?
Kevin (Eng-Platform): If nodes are warm (image cached + model preloaded) scale-up can be <90s for hot-add with our warm-pool. Cold provisioning from zero is ~5–8 minutes. Recommend maintaining a small warm standby (1-2 GPUs) or pre-warm models during predicted windows.
Emily (C-S): Add requirement: audit logs for model selection and routing decisions for compliance review.
Ana (Product): Action items & acceptance criteria for backlog ticket:
- Provide capacity plan doc with math (baseline + burst) and cost estimate (committed vs burst). 
- Define autoscale policy, warm-pool strategy, and cold-start mitigation.
- Define routing policy with model mappings and quality/latency tradeoffs.
- SLA proposal: 99p latency thresholds, uptime, and behavior during over-capacity (fallbacks/queued errors).
- Pilot plan: 2-week pilot with synthetic load + one-week customer pilot; targeted start date by their quarter end.
Jordana (Solutions): I'll prepare an implementation playbook (runbook) for on-call and escalation, plus verification tests.
Mike (Sales): Customer asked for a quick price ballpark today. Can we give a per-month estimate for reserved 4 GPUs + burst 20 GPUs for peak windows (assuming 8 hours/month of bursting)?
Kevin (Eng-Platform): Quick ballpark (very rough): reserved 4 x tier-2 GPUs ~ $Xk/month, burst usage (20 GPUs * 8 hrs) add ~$Yk/month. I'll convert to real pricing in spreadsheet and attach.
Mike (Sales): 👍 Please attach spreadsheet. I'll summarize for FinSolve and check whether they're ok with routing to 35B for latency-critical flows.
deploy-bot: deployment pipeline update: model-warm-pool feature branch deployed to 1903456805
Ana (Product): Thanks team — I'll create the product backlog item with the above acceptance criteria and tag it P1 for this customer. Assigning to Kevin for sizing doc and Jordana for runbook. Emily, can you coordinate pilot sign-up with the customer? 
Emily (C-S): Yep, will coordinate dates and compliance checklist.
Kevin (Eng-Platform): I'll post the sizing spreadsheet in this thread by EOD and link the costing assumptions.
Mike (Sales): Great — copying legal and procurement next. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
